artworks.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
artworks.description: Ingres' Louvre canvas fixes the Theban confrontation: Oedipus answers while the winged woman-lion waits on the rock — bones of failed travellers at their feet. Oil on canvas, Musée du Louvre, Paris.

artworks.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
artworks.description: Moreau's Salon triumph sets the Sphinx clawing at Oedipus' chest — the riddle as Symbolist duel, victory not yet assured. Oil on canvas, Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

artworks.title: The Kiss of the Sphinx
artworks.description: Stuck's Symbolist Sphinx pins a mortal in a lethal embrace — the Theban monster remade as femme fatale, kiss and kill in one gesture. Oil on canvas, Hungarian National Gallery, Budapest.

artworks.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx of Thebes (Attic kylix)
artworks.description: On this Attic red-figure kylix tondo, travelling Oedipus listens as the crowned Sphinx poses her riddle — the Theban monster in its earliest Greek vase form. Ceramic, Vatican Museums (Gregorian Etruscan Museum).

artworks.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
artworks.description: An Attic red-figure amphora shows Oedipus before the Theban Sphinx — the same riddle scene that later painters would enlarge into Romantic and Symbolist drama. Ceramic, Musée du Louvre, Paris.

popCulture.title: Riddle of the Sphinx
popCulture.description: The Theban monster's riddle — four legs, two legs, three — remains the West's stock emblem of a question that kills if unanswered.

popCulture.title: Oedipus and the Sphinx
popCulture.creator: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres
popCulture.description: Ingres' Louvre canvas fixed the modern image of the confrontation — the hero facing the winged woman-lion on the Theban road.
